shill: wifi: Examine assoc/auth status codes at disconnect CL:1226113 uses 802.11 disconnect reasons to generate more suitable shill disconnect reasons. However, assoc/auth status codes are still not used. Of particular importance is when a connection fails due to a pending timeout, as supplicant will always see this as a user disconnect (reason 3). Looking at the assoc/auth status codes provides us with more information, allowing for more accurate shill disconnect reasons. This change also uploads the status codes of assoc/auth failures to UMA. BUG=chromium:625387 TEST=-All unit tests are passing. -Set up AP unable to accept more STAs, and ensured that Shill returned a "too-many-stas" error through its external DBus interface. flash_ec: Have iteflash use I2C through servod with CR50 CCD. Previously flash_ec would instruct iteflash to communicate directly with CR50 when using CCD. Now the same communication path through servod is used with Servo Micro is also used with CR50. Benefits: 1) Allows for resolving b:126189871 without adding significant new complexity in servod. Without this, fixing that bug would involve implementing CR50 I2C USB endpoint disconnect and reconnect commands, exposing them through dut-control, and ensuring they play nicely with I2cPseudoAdapter. With this, that bug can be trivially fixed, and then the retry loop in flash_ec around dut_i2c_mux:ec_prog can be deleted. 2) Simplifies flash_ec with slightly less differences needed in iteflash invocation. BRANCH=none BUG=b:75976718,b:79684405,b:124388894,b:126189871 CQ-DEPEND=CL:1250029,CL:1546592 TEST=The following servo + board combinations were tested: flash_ec -> iteflash -> servo_micro -> bip flash_ec -> iteflash -> servo_v4 -> servo_micro -> bip flash_ec -> iteflash -> servo_v2 -> bip flash_ec -> iteflash -> servo_v4 -> cr50 -> bip Change-Id: I36009b01e45576c786ea78853baf46b52d2232d6 Signed-off-by: Matthew Blecker <matthewb@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1522846 Reviewed-by: Namyoon Woo <namyoon@chromium.org>
